newsitem.title: CANADA: Morrison shares jump on 88 bid.
newsitem.headline: Morrison shares jump on 88 bid.

text.p: Shares in Morrison Petroleums Ltd jumped in heavy volume on Monday after Canadian 88 Energy Corp's announcement of a C$652 million takeover bid for the company.
With Morrison stock trading above the Canadian 88 bid price, investors appeared to be betting on a higher offer.
Morrison shares climbed 1.75 to 10.25 on volume of 4.4 million shares.
Canadian 88, which is smaller than Morrison, said it would offer C$10 for cash, up to C$140 million, or 1.5 Canadian 88 shares for each Morrison share.
Morrison topped actives on the Toronto Stock Exchange.
Morrison said on Friday it was flush with C$180 million in cash after the creation of a royalty trust based on cash flow from an Alberta natural gas plant and a British Columbia oil pipeline.

The company added it would establish a shareholder rights plan to extend the time to consider a takeover offer to 60 days and allow shareholders to acquire common shares at half the market price if a person or group acquired more than 20 percent of Morrison's stock.
Canadian 88 said the bid was conditional on the poison pill being rescinded or ruled ineffective.

Canadian 88 chief executive Greg Noval surprised many in the Canadian energy industry last year by launching an offer for Amerada Hess Canada. Hess Canada was eventually acquired by Petro-Canada in April for C$730 million in a deal that angered Noval.
Morrison, which has shifted its focus to natural gas after being considered more of an oil producer, operates acreage in the southwest Alberta foothills known for deep gas potential.
Canadian 88 last year made a major gas discovery at Waterton on lands next to Morrison's.
